claim: Diebold et al. reported high-dimensional immune profiling of PBMCs from dimethyl fumarate-treated MS patients and proposed a treatment-response monitoring population involving GM-CSF, IFN-gamma, and CXCR3-expressing memory T helper cells.
future_grounding_route: Use as a sharper immune-monitoring comparator; any claim about agreement or conflict with the project's T/B-readable IFN/APC/STAT1 state requires a predefined mapping and rerunnable analysis.

project_finding_reference.finding_id: T/B-readable early IFN/APC/STAT1 monitoring state; Tool-robust but simple V22 scalar

project_use: Sharper external immune-monitoring record for V50 reassessment of compartment-readable DMF response markers.
relationship_note: The source independently supports immune-cell monitoring of DMF response, but it emphasizes a T helper cytokine/CXCR3 population rather than directly validating the project's APC/HLA-II scalar.

source.citation: Diebold et al. High-dimensional immune profiling identifies a biomarker to monitor dimethyl fumarate response in multiple sclerosis. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. 2022.
source.label: Diebold 2022 high-dimensional DMF immune-response monitoring study

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: PNAS article metadata; metadata-only reuse in V50
source_terms.reuse_notes: V50 stores bibliographic/source metadata and a short paraphrased claim only; do not redistribute full article text, figures, or tables.

why_unverifiable: The project has not rerun the mass-cytometry cohorts or spectral-flow validation from the source data.
